PLAN 211.description: Contemporary city development trends, policies, and practices across the globe as explored against the backdrop of culture and technology. Includes hands-on learning.

PLAN 221.description: An exploratory journey through the vast world of visualizing the city and ways of representing the built environment, including how to both interpret and use visualizations to read the city. Prerequisite: Second-year standing or above in any program.

PLAN 231.description: Examination of various approaches to hands-on engagement with urban communities while examining the meaning of public, community, and participation. Prerequisite: Second-year standing.

PLAN 248.description: Selected topics in urban studies. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 321.description: Place-based exploration of the multiple, complex and contested ways urban Indigeneity is constituted in Canada today, with opportunities for field trips and hands-on learning. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or above in any program. Second year students may be admitted with permission of instructor.

PLAN 331.course_name: The Just City in a Divided World
PLAN 331.description: Considers the city as a terrain for the manifestation and mediation of social justice. Explores how the allocation of land, goods, and services in cities (re)produces social stratification, and how institutions and civil society negotiate just and unjust outcomes. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or above in any program. Second year students may be admitted with permission of instructor.

PLAN 341.course_name: Smart Cities: Concepts, Methods and Design
PLAN 341.description: Rapid transformation of cities by information technology and socio-economic innovation; growth in citizen-generated data and the internet of things; emerging theory, methods, and frameworks for understanding Smart Cities. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or above in any program. Second-year students may be admitted with permission of instructor. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 348.description: Selected topics in urban studies. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 351.description: The key social and technological challenges, contradictions, and opportunities in planning for ecologically sound urbanization. Prerequisite: Second-year standing.

PLAN 352.course_name: Planning for Urban Climate and Energy Transitions
PLAN 352.description: Urban planning approaches to mitigating and adapting to climate change with a focus on local-level energy system transitions. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 361.course_name: Community Planning in a World of Diversity
PLAN 361.description: Examination of how the diverse, multicultural, and cosmopolitan aspects of cities create challenges and opportunities for community planning. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

PLAN 372.description: Critical overview of urban housing systems and policy tools for housing justice. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 425.description: Evolution, practice and future of urban planning and development, with emphasis on institutional arrangements, housing, transportation, urban design and development control. For third- and fourth-year undergraduate students interested in urban planning. [3-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 452.description: Application of key elements of urban studies theory, concepts, and methods to a community-engaged urban challenge. Prerequisite: GEOG 451. Fourth-year standing. Equivalency: URST452

PLAN 461.description: The role of urban planning and policy in producing social and environmental conditions for health equity. Restricted to students in the Bachelor of Arts Major in Urban Studies with at least fourth-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 532.course_name: Strategic Planning: Developing and Implementing Policy Plans
PLAN 532.description: Theory and practice of developing and implementing plans for sustainable regions, cities, and neighbourhoods. Combining land use, transportation, environment, socio-economic, and financial directions, managing plan making including public participation, and writing council reports. PLAN 535.description: Foundations of urban travel modelling: data needs; survey and sampling techniques; model calibration and validation; discrete choice modeling; 4-step travel demand forecasting (trip generation, distribution, modal choice, and assignment); activity based models; integrated land use/transport models. Credit will be granted for only one of CIVL_V 441, CIVL_V 583, or PLAN_V 535. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 542.description: Approach, role, style, and essential skills of practical urban planning: working at the community level; developing overall policy; managing development; undertaking urban design; and engaging in the political process. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 559.description: Research design for SCARP thesis-based Master's students. Approaches for designing research methodologies and thesis structure. PLAN 579.course_name: Public Health, Transportation, and the Built Environment
PLAN 579.description: Health issues associated with transportation and the built environment; design of urban form for non-motorized transportation for the improvement of personal and environmental health; factors that impact transportation choices; applying findings from research to specific transportation planning processes and projects. Credit will be granted for only one of PLAN_V 579 or SPPH_V 571. Equivalency: SPPH_V 571. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 580.description: Topics include the relationship between transportation and urban activity systems; analysis of supply and demand; accessibility and environment; institutional arrangements and public finance. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 583.description: Homes and communities are a focus of public policy for local and senior governments. Overview of past and current policies addressing the design and development of homes and communities. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 587.description: A studio/seminar on the history of the physical form of cities and theories of city design. Topics include social impacts, heritage and environmental conservation, urban revitalization, and the legal and administrative instruments for the implementation of city designs. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 591.description: Identify potential impacts of human land use activities on environmental systems; review policies in place at various levels of government in Canada (and elsewhere) that promote sustainable development and reduce negative impacts; assess effectiveness of those policies; design new policies. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

PLAN 597.description: The relationships among relevant bio-physical, socio-economic and institutional systems as applied to regional planning for watersheds, lakes, estuaries, coastal zones and international river basins. Water supply, waste disposal, fisheries, aquaculture, recreation, hydropower and flood control. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
